01 Biography

Shuzhi Sam Ge, Fellows of SAEng, IEEE, IFAC, IET, ACA, AAIA, CAA and PEB. Professor, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. He received his Ph.D. and DIC from Imperial College London, U.K., in January and July 1993 respectively, and his B.Sc. degree from the Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Beijing, China, in 1986. His current research interests include intelligent control, artificial intelligence, robotics, and research translation.

He serves as President of the Asian Control Association (2024–2026), IFAC Council Member (2023–2029), Singapore Lead and Asian Co-lead of INPACE, and Founding Editor-in-Chief of the International Journal of Social Robotics. He previously served as Vice President for Technical Activites (2009-2010) and Membership Activities (2011-2012) of the IEEE Control Systems Society.

He has received major honours incl. Singapore National Technology Award, Inaugural Temasek Young Investigator Award on Intelligent Control of Unmanned Vehicles, IEEE CSS Distinguished Member Award, AI Singapore Grand Challenge Award in Robust AI. He has authored 10 monographs and 800+ publications, with 70,000+ citations and an h-index of 126 as of March 2026 and was a Clarivate Highly Cited Researcher for 10 consecutive years (2016–2025). He has led as (co-)PI or participated in 20+ research grants.

02 Research & Projects

Research

Embodied Intelligence and Robot LearningView 3 representative papers⌄

Connecting perception, learning and action through the dynamics of physical robots. Representative work spans learning from human interaction, compliance in uncertain environments and safe reinforcement learning for autonomous vehicles.

  2. Human–Robot Collaboration Based on Motion Intention Estimation ↗IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics · 2014Motion-intention estimation for physical collaboration.
  3. Learning compliance control of robot manipulators in contact with the unknown environment ↗2010 IEEE International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering · 2010Learning compliant behaviour during contact with an unknown environment.
Social Robotics and Human-Robot InteractionView 3 representative papers⌄

Developing robots that understand and respond to people through intention estimation, affective interaction and socially aware navigation. The focus is on how robotic behaviour can support natural, cooperative interaction.

  1. Role playing learning for socially concomitant mobile robot navigation ↗CAAI Transactions on Intelligence Technology · 2018Role-playing learning for socially aware companion navigation.
  2. Human–Robot Collaboration Based on Motion Intention Estimation ↗IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics · 2014Motion-intention estimation for physical collaboration.
  3. Active affective facial analysis for human-robot interaction ↗RO-MAN 2008 - The 17th IEEE International Symposium on Robot and Human Interactive Communication · 2008Affective facial analysis for human–robot interaction.
Robust and Secure Autonomous SystemsView 3 representative papers⌄

Designing autonomous and networked systems that account for uncertainty, communication limits and security. Recent work develops coded and event-triggered control, alongside stability analysis for coordinated multiagent behaviour.

  1. Secure Asymptotic Consensus Control for MASs ↗IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control · 2026Secure asymptotic consensus in multiagent systems.
  2. Rate-Coded Secure Control for Multiagent Systems ↗IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control · 2025Rate-coded communication for secure distributed control.
  3. Coded event-triggered control for nonlinear systems ↗Automatica · 2024Coded event-triggered feedback for nonlinear systems.
Safety-Critical and Constrained ControlView 3 representative papers⌄

Making state, output and actuator limits explicit in the control design. Barrier Lyapunov Functions, adaptive tracking and safe learning connect constraint satisfaction with closed-loop stability under the assumptions of each design.

  1. Barrier Lyapunov Function-Based Safe Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicles With Optimized Backstepping ↗IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems · 2024Combining reinforcement learning, backstepping and safety constraints.
  2. Barrier Lyapunov functions for the control of output-constrained nonlinear systems ↗Automatica, 45(4), 918–927 · 2009Barrier Lyapunov Functions for output-constrained nonlinear control.
  3. Adaptive tracking control of uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems with input constraints ↗Automatica, 47(3), 452–465 · 2011Adaptive tracking with explicit actuator-input constraints.
Adaptive Neural ControlView 3 representative papers⌄

Combining neural-network approximation with adaptive and Lyapunov-based control for uncertain nonlinear dynamics. The research develops stable learning and tracking methods for strict-feedback systems, MIMO systems and nonlinear actuator behaviour.

  1. Adaptive neural control of uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems ↗IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks, 15(3), 674–692 · 2004Adaptive neural control of uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems.
  2. Adaptive neural network control for strict-feedback nonlinear systems using backstepping design ↗Automatica, 36(12), 1835–1846 · 2000Backstepping-based neural control of strict-feedback dynamics.
  3. Robust adaptive neural network control for a class of uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems with input nonlinearities ↗IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks, 21(5), 796–812 · 2010Robust neural control in the presence of input nonlinearities.

Projects

Development of Stable Robust and Secure Intelligent Systems for Autonomous Vehicles ↗

Principal Investigator · AI Singapore Grand Challenge Award in Robust AI · 2023–2026

Ge leads the award-winning programme “Development of Stable Robust and Secure Intelligent Systems for Autonomous Vehicles” under the AI Singapore Grand Challenge Award in Robust AI. The project brings together expertise in stable control, machine learning and generative AI to address a central challenge for physical AI: maintaining dependable perception when an autonomous vehicle encounters unfamiliar conditions or adversarial interference.

The research develops multimodal defence using complementary visual and LiDAR information, together with unified spatio-temporal refinement to improve detection stability and physical plausibility. These directions connect learning-based perception with the structure of the physical world. Digital-twin simulation and physical trials support the investigation of stable, robust and secure autonomy.

MR2 — Modular Reconfigurable Mobile Robots

Team PI · A*STAR · 2025–2028

MR2 develops a modular approach to mobile robotics: interchangeable chassis, actuation, navigation and payload modules allow a platform to be configured around the needs of a task. The architecture is designed to support customization, repair, upgrades and reuse, helping connect robot design with practical deployment requirements.

As Team PI, Ge addresses the modelling and control challenges that arise when a robot’s mechanical configuration changes. This includes configuration-aware dynamic modelling, intelligent trajectory tracking and control allocation for heterogeneous wheel arrangements. The research connects the physical design of a reconfigurable robot with control methods that account for its assembled dynamics, extending adaptive intelligent control towards flexible robotic platforms.

Social Robots: Breathing Life Into Machines

Principal Investigator · MDA / NRF · 2007–2012

As Principal Investigator of “Social Robots: Breathing Life Into Machines”, Ge developed a programme centred on robots that communicate with people and participate in human environments. Adam provides a physical embodiment of this direction, connecting social interaction with intelligent robotic behaviour.

The broader research examines human intention, affective cues and cooperative behaviour, linking physical human–robot interaction with social awareness. Ge’s leadership also extends to building the field’s international community through the International Journal of Social Robotics and the International Conference on Social Robotics. Together, the research programme and these academic platforms support the development of social robotics across engineering, human interaction and societal applications.

INPACE: INdo-PACific-European Hub for Digital Partnerships ↗

Singapore Lead and Asian Co-lead · Horizon Europe · 2024–2027

As Singapore Lead and Asian Co-lead of INPACE, Ge contributes to a Horizon Europe initiative connecting Europe and the Indo-Pacific through digital partnerships. The programme brings together research, industry and policy communities around artificial intelligence, future chips, networks and trustworthy digital technologies, supporting cooperation with Singapore, Japan, the Republic of Korea and India.

Ge chaired the EU–Indo-Pacific Digital Partnership Conference 2025 in Singapore, bringing policymakers, researchers, innovators and industry leaders into a shared discussion of digital cooperation. This work connects technical research with international collaboration, helping participating communities exchange priorities, identify complementary expertise and develop sustained partnerships.

03 Selected Publications

2009— citations
Constrained control

Barrier Lyapunov functions for the control of output-constrained nonlinear systems ↗

Tee, K. P., Ge, S. S., & Tay, E. H.

Automatica, 45(4), 918–927.

Pioneered the use of Barrier Lyapunov Functions for output-constrained nonlinear control, embedding constraint enforcement directly in the stability analysis. By making the Lyapunov function grow unbounded as the output approaches a prescribed boundary, the design links bounded closed-loop behaviour to satisfaction of the output constraint under the paper’s assumptions. This work gives a constructive mathematical route from conventional tracking control to control with explicit safety limits, and provides a foundation for subsequent research on constrained intelligent systems.

2005— citations
Switched systems

Switched linear systems: control and design ↗

Sun, Z., & Ge, S. S.

Springer London.

Established a systematic treatment of switched linear systems, bringing controllability, observability, stability and control design into a common framework. The monograph develops geometric and algebraic characterizations that reveal how switching changes what a system can achieve, together with methods for designing switching laws and feedback controllers. Its contribution is to make the interaction between continuous dynamics and discrete switching amenable to verifiable analysis, providing a theoretical basis for the design of hybrid control systems.

2013— citations
Stable neural control

Stable adaptive neural network control ↗

Ge, S. S., Hang, C. C., Lee, T. H., & Zhang, T.

Springer Science & Business Media. 2013 eBook.

Developed a systematic foundation for stable adaptive neural-network control of uncertain nonlinear systems. The monograph connects the approximation capabilities of neural networks with Lyapunov-based controller design, so that adaptation is analysed as part of the closed-loop dynamics. It addresses the central challenge of obtaining useful learning behaviour while establishing stability and tracking properties. This framework helped make neural control a mathematically grounded approach to systems whose nonlinear dynamics cannot be modelled precisely in advance.

2011— citations
Input constraints

Adaptive tracking control of uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems with input constraints ↗

Chen, M., Ge, S. S., & Ren, B.

Automatica, 47(3), 452–465.

Extended adaptive tracking control to uncertain multi-input multi-output nonlinear systems with constrained actuator inputs. The design explicitly accounts for input saturation through an auxiliary system, integrating the actuator limitation into the adaptive-control analysis. This addresses a practical gap between unconstrained control laws and the finite authority of physical actuators. The result links tracking performance, uncertainty compensation and input constraints within one design framework, with boundedness properties established under the assumptions stated in the paper.

2004— citations
MIMO nonlinear control

Adaptive neural control of uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems ↗

Ge, S. S., & Wang, C.

IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks, 15(3), 674–692.

Developed adaptive neural control for coupled, uncertain multi-input multi-output nonlinear systems. By exploiting the system’s block-triangular structure, the work constructs controllers for classes of systems in which nonlinear coupling makes direct inversion difficult. Neural approximation is combined with stability analysis to establish semiglobal uniform ultimate boundedness while avoiding controller singularities for the considered classes. It advances the broader programme of extending intelligent adaptive control from simpler single-channel models to interacting nonlinear systems.

2000— citations
Adaptive backstepping

Adaptive neural network control for strict-feedback nonlinear systems using backstepping design ↗

Zhang, T., Ge, S. S., & Hang, C. C.

Automatica, 36(12), 1835–1846.

Combined neural-network approximation with recursive backstepping design for uncertain strict-feedback nonlinear systems. At successive stages of the design, neural models compensate for unknown nonlinear functions while a Lyapunov argument links the stages into a closed-loop stability analysis. The paper provides a constructive method for developing adaptive controllers when an accurate plant model is unavailable. It forms part of the theoretical foundation for later work on learning-based nonlinear control, including efforts to manage the complexity of recursive controller design.

1998— citations
Robot control

Adaptive neural network control of robotic manipulators ↗

Ge, S. S., Lee, T. H., & Harris, C. J.

World Scientific.

Connected the physical structure of robotic manipulators with adaptive neural-network control. The monograph brings robot dynamics, neural approximation and Lyapunov-based analysis together to address control in the presence of uncertain nonlinear dynamics. Its significance lies in treating learning and mechanical-system stability as parts of the same control problem, rather than assessing approximation quality alone. This provides a theoretical foundation for intelligent robot control that retains an explicit connection to the structure and behaviour of the physical machine.

2010— citations
Robust neural control

Robust adaptive neural network control for a class of uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems with input nonlinearities ↗

Chen, M., Ge, S. S., & How, B. V. E.

IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks, 21(5), 796–812.

Addressed uncertain multi-input multi-output nonlinear systems in which the actuator input itself is nonlinear. The paper combines robust adaptive design with neural-network approximation to compensate for uncertainty while analysing the stability of the resulting closed loop. By treating input nonlinearities within the control problem, it extends the applicability of adaptive neural control beyond ideal actuator models. This contributes to the development of intelligent controllers that account for both uncertain plant dynamics and non-ideal actuation under stated modelling assumptions.

2011— citations
Switched-system stability

Stability theory of switched dynamical systems ↗

Sun, Z., & Ge, S. S.

Springer London.

Developed a unified account of stability analysis for switched dynamical systems, examining how the dynamics of individual subsystems interact with the switching signal. The monograph distinguishes stability under different switching conditions and relates analytical criteria to the design of stabilizing switching strategies. Its importance is in showing why subsystem-level properties alone do not settle the stability of the combined system, and in providing systematic tools for reasoning about hybrid dynamics and constructing switching laws with verifiable stability properties.
